tagline: Handmade potato soap that helps fade tan and dark spots — gently, without harsh bleach.
description: Sun, dust and pollution leave skin looking dull, tanned and patchy. Velvet Potato is a handmade soap made with raw potato juice — the desi remedy for tan and dark spots — blended with olive oil, glycerin and calming lavender.

Potato's natural enzyme (catecholase), vitamin C and gentle lactic acid help shed dead skin cells and clear impurities from your pores. With regular use it helps fade sun tan, dark spots, acne marks and uneven patches, and brings back your natural glow — without harsh bleaching agents.

Potato starch soaks up excess oil, so it's a great match for oily and combination skin, while olive oil and glycerin keep skin soft and balanced instead of tight and dry. Each bar is handmade in a pretty flower shape — lovely to use, lovely to gift.
highlights: Handmade with raw potato juice, olive oil & glycerin
Helps fade sun tan, dark spots & acne marks with regular use
Gentle exfoliation for smoother, brighter-looking skin
Controls excess oil & cleans pores — great for oily or combination skin
No harsh bleaching agents · soothing lavender scent
specs: Raw potato juice, olive oil, catecholase (potato enzyme), vitamin C, lactic acid, glycerin, lavender essential oil
Oily, combination & dull skin — face and body
Tan & dark-spot fading, gentle exfoliation, oil control, soothing, hydration balance
faqs: Is it really handmade?
Yes. Every bar is handmade, so the shape and natural speckles vary slightly from bar to bar.
How soon will I see results?
Skin feels fresh and less oily from the first wash. Tan, dark spots and acne marks fade gradually with daily use over a few weeks — results vary from person to person.
Can I use it on my face?
Yes, it's made for face and body. Lather it up, massage gently for 30–60 seconds, rinse, and follow with a moisturiser.
Is it suitable for sensitive skin?
It has no harsh bleaching agents, but it does contain mild lactic acid and lavender oil. If your skin is sensitive, do a small patch test first and avoid broken or irritated skin.
How should I store it?
Keep it on a dry, draining soap dish between uses so the bar stays firm and lasts longer.
